parsed.explanation: The quoted sentence correctly identifies a fatal gap: to obtain D(M)=μ−D(R)≤1, Xiang must force D(R)≥μ−1, but no preceding argument does so. The later pairing/binary strategy merely asserts that an arbitrary initial partition can be refined into equal pairs plus a leftover 1; it neither constructs those cuts for arbitrary real segment lengths nor proves the claimed n-cut budget. The small-n checks and numerical optimization do not establish the universal all-n upper bound. A substantive construction such as the ledger’s subset-sum pigeonhole and mirrored-cut argument is required.
